entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3426"/><div sID="gen4826" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3426"/><hi type="bold">4-6. the king talked with Gehazi--</hi>Ceremonial pollution being conveyed by contact alone, there was nothing to prevent a conference being held with this leper at a distance; and although he was excluded from the town of Samaria, this reported conversation may have taken place at the gate or in one of the royal gardens. The providence of God so ordained that King Jehoram had been led to inquire, with great interest, into the miraculous deeds of Elisha, and that the prophet's servant was in the act of relating the marvellous incident of the restoration of the Shunammite's son when she made her appearance to prefer her request. The king was pleased to grant it; and a state officer was charged to afford her every facility in the recovery of her family possession out of the hands of the occupier.<div eID="gen4826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4827" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2Kgs.8.7-2Kgs.8.15">2Ki 8:7-15</reference>. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3427"/><div sID="gen4828" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3427"/><hi type="bold">7-8. Elisha came to Damascus--</hi>He was directed thither by the Spirit of God, in pursuance of the mission formerly given to his master in Horeb (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.19.15">1Ki 19:15</reference>), to anoint Hazael king of Syria. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3430"/><div sID="gen4832" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3430"/><hi type="bold">11. he settled his countenance stedfastly until he was ashamed--</hi>that is, Hazael. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3431"/><div sID="gen4833" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3431"/><hi type="bold">15. took a thick cloth, &c.--</hi>a coverlet. In the East, this article of bedding is generally a thick quilt of wool or cotton, so that, with its great weight, when steeped in water, it would be a fit instrument for accomplishing the murderous purpose, without leaving any marks of violence. It has been supposed by many doubtful that Hazael purposely murdered the king. But it is common for Eastern people to sleep with their faces covered with a mosquito net; and, in some cases of fever, they dampen the bedclothes. Hazael, aware of those chilling remedies being usually resorted to, might have, with an honest intention, spread a refreshing cover over him. The rapid occurrence of the king's death and immediate burial were favorable to his instant elevation to the throne.<div eID="gen4833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4834" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2Kgs.8.16-2Kgs.8.23">2Ki 8:16-23</reference>. Jehoram's Wicked Reign. <div eID="gen4834" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3433"/><div sID="gen4836" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3433"/><hi type="bold">18. daughter of Ahab--</hi>Athaliah, through whose influence Jehoram introduced the worship of Baal and many other evils into the kingdom of Judah (see <reference osisRef="2Chr.21.2-2Chr.21.20">2Ch 21:2-20</reference>). This apostasy would have led to the total extinction of the royal family in that kingdom, had it not been for the divine promise to David (<reference osisRef="2Sam.7.16">2Sa 7:16</reference>). A national chastisement, however, was inflicted on Judah by the revolt of Edom, which, being hitherto governed by a tributary ruler (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.3.9">2Ki 3:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Kgs.22.47">1Ki 22:47</reference>), erected the standard of independence (<reference osisRef="2Chr.21.9">2Ch 21:9</reference>).<div eID="gen4836" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4837" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2Kgs.8.24">2Ki 8:24</reference>. Ahaziah Succeeds Him. <div eID="gen4837" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 18. daughter of Ahab-- Athaliah, through whose influence Jehoram introduced the worship of Baal and many other evils into the kingdom of Judah (see 2Ch 21:2-20 ). This apostasy would have led to the total extinction of the royal family in that kingdom, had it not been for the divine promise to David ( 2Sa 7:16 ). A national chastisement, however, was inflicted on Judah by the revolt of Edom, which, being hitherto governed by a tributary ruler ( 2Ki 3:9 ; 1Ki 22:47 ), erected the standard of independence ( 2Ch 21:9 ). 2Ki 8:24 . Ahaziah Succeeds Him.
